records.summary: A consumer charge ledger would identify recurring charges and provide country-aware cancellation and refund routes. It addresses charges users say they did not expect or cannot work out how to cancel.
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster records 5 paying proofs, but the supplied examples are complaints and do not specify verified revenue or pricing for this product.

competitors.price: Free for up to five subscriptions

competitors.name: Apple
competitors.note: Provides purchase history, subscription management, and charge/refund routes for charges on its platform.

competitors.name: Google
competitors.note: Provides purchase history, subscription management, and charge/refund routes for charges on its platform.

rounds.plain: K2: at least two relevant launches were found in the last six months. K0: the basic tracker and reminder features appear easy to copy, and no exclusive data asset was identified.

risks: Apple and Google already handle some purchase history, subscription management, and charge/refund needs on their platforms.
Agent-work and weekly-hours constraints remain unverified.
records.moat: No clear moat: the core tracker and reminder functions are readily copied, and merchants and payment platforms control the underlying billing and refund records.

records.summary: A consumer cloud-rescue tool would help people retrieve or move files from an over-quota cloud account to another provider. The evidence describes users who say they cannot access files or photos when storage is full.
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster records 5 paying proofs, but the supplied examples are complaints and do not establish verified revenue or pricing for this product.

competitors.note: Provides cloud import; added OneDrive support announced on 20 Oct 2026.

competitors.name: EchoFile
competitors.note: Announced a cloud-to-cloud transfer pilot on 13 Oct 2026.

competitors.name: Enter Space
competitors.note: Listed as launched in October 2026; exact day unverified.

rounds.plain: K2: multiple relevant category launches surfaced recently. K0: existing tools cover the core functions and no exclusive asset was identified. K3: Dropbox already documents web downloads for part of the access need.

risks: The overlap between broader cloud-access products and over-quota rescue is described as a category-level inference.
Agent-work and weekly-hours constraints remain unverified.
records.moat: No distinct moat was identified. Cloud providers and existing transfer or mounting tools already offer core access and migration functions; no exclusive data asset was identified.

records.summary: A consumer sync health and conflict-recovery utility would show stale folders and safe recovery steps across services such as Dropbox, OneDrive, and iCloud. The proposed product aims to help users diagnose and recover from file-sync problems across devices.
records.customer: Consumers syncing files across devices and services
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster records 1 paying proof. One supplied complaint says the reviewer stopped subscribing after sync problems, while another says Dropbox mobile files do not sync with desktop files.

competitors.name: SyncApp for OneDrive
competitors.note: Official press kit says it launches May 2026; homepage says it is shipping now, but exact store launch date is unverified.

competitors.name: Skymir
competitors.note: Listed as launched on 10 Oct 2026; described as two-way Google Drive sync for Linux.

rounds.plain: K0: a three-month build scope, copy barrier, and unowned asset were not demonstrated. K2: two relevant launches surfaced. K3: Apple, Google, and Microsoft already provide first-party sync. K4: at least five free or open-source alternatives serve the core need without a clear wedge.

risks: Coverage across providers would require integrations and permissions, and cluster-wide coverage within three months is unverified.
The proposed product's ≥50% agent-work and ≤5 h/week limits are not established.
records.moat: No distinct, unowned asset or clear copy barrier was identified; platform and storage providers already serve the core sync function.
